content: The plasma levels of ethinyl estradiol may be altered by various drug interactions, leading to changes in its efficacy and potential contraceptive failure. Below are detailed descriptions of these interactions: 1. Lorlantinib reduces the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction may compromise the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. It is recommended to use a non-hormonal contraceptive method and monitor closely. 2. Lumacaftor/Ivacaftor decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol through an unspecified mechanism. Hormonal contraceptives are not reliable in this context, and alternative or additional contraceptive methods should be used. Co-administration should be avoided unless the benefits outweigh the risks. Monitor for increased menstrual-related adverse effects such as amenorrhea, dysmenorrhea, or menorrhagia. 3. Lumefantrine reduces the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Etynodiol increases the levels of maraviroc by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially leading to increased toxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Mavacamten decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This may lead to contraceptive failure or breakthrough bleeding. Patients should use a contraceptive method unaffected by CYP450 enzyme induction, such as an intrauterine system, or add a non-hormonal contraceptive like condoms during co-administration and for four months after the last mavacamten dose. 6. Ethinyl estradiol reduces the effects of metformin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Metronidazole decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 8. Metyrapone has reduced efficacy when co-administered with estrogens, including oral contraceptives, due to an unspecified interaction mechanism. Discontinuation of estrogens prior to and during metyrapone administration may be advisable. 9. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of mexiletine by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of midazolam by decreasing its metabolism. This interaction may prolong sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Mifepristone decreases the effects of etynodiol and ethinyl estradiol through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Additionally, mifepristone increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 12. Mineral oil decreases the levels of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is minor or unknown, but monitoring is recommended. 13. Minocycline decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 14. Mitotane decreases the levels of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Mitotane is a strong inducer of CYP3A4, and dosage adjustments of CYP3A4 substrates may be necessary. Monitor closely. 15. Momelotinib increases the toxicity of ethinyl estradiol by competing for plasma protein binding. Momelotinib, as a BCRP inhibitor, may increase the exposure of BCRP substrates, necessitating dosage adjustments. Monitor closely. 16. Moxifloxacin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 17. Mycophenolate decreases the effects of ethinyl estradiol through an unknown mechanism. Patients should consider using an alternative or additional form of contraception. 18. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Ethinyl estradiol increases the effects of naratriptan through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 20. Nefazodone increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 21. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 22. Nemolizumab decreases the levels of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Dosage modification may be needed. Monitor closely. 23. Neomycin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 24. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 25. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of nicardipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of nilotinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Nirmatrelvir decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by increasing its metabolism. Consider using additional non-hormonal contraceptive methods for the remainder of the cycle. 28. Nitrofurantoin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 29. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of nortriptyline through an unspecified mechanism. This may lead to increased antidepressant serum concentrations and potential adverse effects. Monitor closely. 30. Ofloxacin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 31. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of olanzapine by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Ombitasvir/Paritaprevir/Ritonavir and Dasabuvir significantly increase the toxicity of ethinyl estradiol through an unspecified mechanism. Discontinue ethinyl estradiol-containing medications before initiating this combination therapy. 33. Otesecazole increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting BCRP. Use the lowest starting dose of BCRP substrates or consider reducing their dose. Monitor closely. 34. Oxcarbazepine decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 35. Paromomycin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 36. Penicillin G decreases the levels of ethinyl estradiol by increasing its metabolism. Monitor closely for the risk of contraceptive failure. 37. Penicillin VK decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 38. Pentobarbital decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 39. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 40. Phenytoin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 41. Pioglitazone decreases the levels of ethinyl estradiol through an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Primidone decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 44. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of protriptyline through an unspecified mechanism. This may lead to increased antidepressant serum concentrations and potential adverse effects. Monitor closely. 45. Quinidine increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting P-glycoprotein efflux transporters. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 46. Quinupristin/Dalfopristin increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of ramelteon by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Ranolazine increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 49. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of rasagiline by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Repotrectinib decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 51. Ribociclib increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 52. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 53. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs.
